title: ImplementationCandidate v0.1
description: What an agent emits INSTEAD of writing Terraform: capability attributes with provenance, verified against a contract. Provider detail rides in the free-form implementation block (D26) — ignored by the verifier, consumed by the compiler, never the source of truth (D18: the compiler re-derives attributes from its own output and verification runs again).
$comment: closed at the root (D1170): the runtime refuses a top-level key it does not read, and until this was written the published schema did not — a `constraint:` (singular) block, the exact defect D673 refused, validated here without a word. `x-` is the escape, on both sides.

^x-.$comment: the escape a document uses for data the runtime deliberately does not read

additionalProperties.$comment: closed: the four keys below are the whole shape of a capability block. `implementation` is the free-form half (D26) and an operand no driver reads is refused there; a key at THIS level is structure, and one the loader does not read is a stated intent nothing acts on. Written one floor too high, an operand used to seal a plan at exit 0 while the resource kept its default (D1160).

implementation.description: Free-form provider detail (tiers, disk types, flags). The verifier ignores it; the compiler consumes it (D26). An operand VALUE may instead be an intra-plan output reference — a mapping whose sole key is `$ref` (D226/#/$defs/outputRef) — resolved to another same-candidate capability's typed output; the compiler never coerces it into a string. Every operand value is RECORDED IN THE LEDGER VERBATIM and stays there for the life of that ledger; capsules and exports carry it onward. Do not put a credential in one. groundhold warns when a value has the SHAPE of a credential (D364), but that detector is deliberately narrow — a pattern that fires on ordinary configuration teaches people to ignore it — so it cannot recognise an arbitrary random secret, and its silence is not a clearance. Where an operand is the only channel to the target (an EventBridge Scheduler payload reaches the target exactly as written, with no header channel available), the secret belongs in a secret manager the TARGET resolves for itself, so that only its name is written here (D851).

scalar.description: Typed scalar (D3, D15): bool; number; string with unit syntax — duration '5m', money '912 EUR', percent '99.9%', bytes '100GiB'/'100GB', protocol 'postgresql/16'; money object {amount, currency}; or a list of scalars.

attributeValue.description: A plain scalar is shorthand for status: declared. A mapping with a status key carries explicit provenance (D5).

outputRef.$comment: descriptive-only: the `implementation:` block is free-form by D26, so this shape is PUBLISHED for an author to write against and deliberately not enforced by this schema. Declared, because an unreferenced definition otherwise reads as an oversight — and one of those had silently drifted out of step with the runtime by the time anyone looked (D1158).
outputRef.description: Intra-plan output reference (D226/F13): an implementation operand whose value is another same-candidate capability's typed output, wired in the SAME plan. Structured, never string interpolation (invariant #4). `$ref` MUST be the sole key; `capability` is a capID in this candidate; `output` must appear in that capability's driver OutputsFor and match the operand slot's kind (no coercion, invariant #2).

provenanced.$comment: closed (D1161): a typo here — `confidance` — dropped the confidence and the document passed at exit 0, so an assumption's strength vanished silently.
